questions.stem: A 2-month-old infant has poor feeding, tachypnea, diaphoresis with feeds, and fewer wet diapers for 2 days. He had diarrhea 1 week ago. Heart rate is 172/min, respiratory rate 58/min, and temperature 37.1°C. Examination shows a gallop, hepatomegaly, and cool feet. Which finding most strongly argues against uncomplicated bronchiolitis and toward cardiac disease?
questions.rationale: Hepatomegaly plus a gallop is a classic pediatric heart-failure combination and is not explained by uncomplicated bronchiolitis.

option_explanations.A: Viral symptoms occur in both bronchiolitis and myocarditis.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Systemic venous congestion and an abnormal cardiac exam point to heart failure.
option_explanations.D: Young age increases risk from many illnesses but is not specific.
option_explanations.E: Poor intake is common in both respiratory and cardiac disease.

questions.board_pearl: Hepatomegaly is an important heart-failure clue in infants with respiratory symptoms.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl has fatigue, dyspnea, and chest discomfort after a viral illness. Troponin is elevated and BNP is markedly elevated. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: The tests prove a specific viral etiology
options.B: The combination supports myocardial injury and hemodynamic stress but is not diagnostic by itself
options.C: A high BNP excludes pericardial involvement
options.D: Troponin elevation establishes a need for coronary angiography
options.E: Normal creatine kinase would exclude myocarditis

questions.rationale: Troponin supports myocardial injury and BNP/NT-proBNP supports cardiac wall stress/heart failure, but neither is specific enough to independently establish cause.

option_explanations.A: Biomarkers do not identify the pathogen.
option_explanations.B: Correct. They strengthen the clinical case but must be interpreted with ECG, imaging, and examination.
option_explanations.C: BNP does not rule out pericardial inflammation.
option_explanations.D: Troponin elevation in a child has multiple causes and does not automatically mandate angiography.
option_explanations.E: CK is not sufficiently sensitive to exclude myocarditis.

questions.board_pearl: Use cardiac biomarkers as supportive evidence, not as stand-alone diagnostic proof.

questions.stem: An 11-year-old boy has suspected myocarditis with elevated troponin and mild LV systolic dysfunction. Blood pressure is normal, but telemetry shows frequent ventricular premature beats. Which disposition is most appropriate?

options.B: Observation at home with activity restriction

questions.rationale: Myocarditis can deteriorate rapidly and ventricular ectopy indicates electrical instability that warrants inpatient monitoring.

option_explanations.A: Does not provide adequate rhythm surveillance.
option_explanations.B: Home observation is unsafe given myocardial dysfunction and ventricular ectopy.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Continuous monitoring allows prompt recognition of malignant arrhythmias or worsening function.
option_explanations.D: A Holter may be useful later but does not substitute for acute inpatient monitoring.
option_explanations.E: Follow-up that remote ignores current risk.

questions.board_pearl: Electrical instability is a reason to monitor suspected myocarditis closely even when blood pressure is initially normal.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child with myocarditis has cool extremities, delayed capillary refill, narrow pulse pressure, hepatomegaly, and pulmonary crackles. Which physiologic abnormality best explains the overall picture?

options.B: Reduced myocardial contractility causing low cardiac output and congestion

questions.rationale: Depressed contractility lowers forward output while elevating filling pressures, producing poor perfusion and systemic/pulmonary congestion.

option_explanations.A: The clinical signs indicate low, not high, output.
option_explanations.B: Correct. It integrates the perfusion and congestion findings.
option_explanations.C: Pulmonary vasodilation does not explain systemic low output.
option_explanations.E: Erythropoietin is unrelated to the acute hemodynamics.

questions.board_pearl: Myocarditis can cause simultaneous low forward flow and backward congestion.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy has chest pain after a viral syndrome. Troponin is elevated. ECG shows focal ST elevation. Echocardiography shows a regional wall-motion abnormality but no coronary origin abnormality. Which test is most useful to distinguish inflammatory myocardial injury from an ischemic pattern?
questions.rationale: CMR can distinguish typical nonischemic myocarditis patterns from subendocardial or territorial ischemic injury.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Tissue characterization and injury distribution directly address the differential.
option_explanations.C: Does not explain troponin elevation and ST changes.
option_explanations.E: Not relevant to the myocardial differential.

questions.board_pearl: Regional ECG or echo abnormalities do not exclude myocarditis; CMR can clarify tissue pattern.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old child develops rapidly progressive heart failure, hypotension, sustained ventricular arrhythmias, and worsening end-organ perfusion despite intensive support. Which circumstance most strongly increases the potential value of endomyocardial biopsy?

options.A: Mild isolated chest pain with normal function
options.B: A stable child whose symptoms are resolving
options.C: Fulminant unexplained heart failure in which a specific histologic diagnosis could alter therapy
options.E: A normal ECG after a viral illness

questions.rationale: Biopsy is not routine for every suspected case, but it becomes more relevant in fulminant or refractory presentations when identifying entities such as giant-cell or eosinophilic myocarditis could change treatment.

option_explanations.A: The procedural risk is not justified in a mild stable presentation.
option_explanations.B: Resolving disease usually does not require invasive tissue diagnosis.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Severe refractory disease with possible treatment-changing histology is a classic high-value scenario.
option_explanations.D: Troponin elevation alone is insufficient indication.
option_explanations.E: A normal ECG does not create a biopsy indication.

questions.board_pearl: Biopsy has greatest value when the result could change management in severe or atypical disease.

questions.stem: A 7-month-old infant with tachypnea and poor feeding receives two fluid boluses for presumed dehydration. He becomes more tachypneic and develops crackles and hepatomegaly. Which diagnosis should rise most sharply on the differential?

options.B: Acute myocardial dysfunction with heart failure

questions.rationale: Worsening respiratory distress after volume expansion plus crackles and hepatomegaly suggests limited cardiac reserve with congestion rather than simple dehydration.

option_explanations.A: Would not explain new pulmonary/systemic congestion after fluids.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Fluid intolerance is a clue to pump dysfunction.
option_explanations.C: Croup causes upper-airway findings, not hepatomegaly.
option_explanations.D: Aspiration would not cause systemic venous congestion.
option_explanations.E: Anemia may cause tachycardia but not acute volume-sensitive heart failure findings.

questions.board_pearl: Clinical worsening after fluid can reveal occult myocardial dysfunction.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old girl with acute myocarditis has no evidence of bacterial infection, autoimmune disease, toxin exposure, or structural heart disease. Which etiologic principle is most appropriate for general pediatric practice?

options.A: A viral or postinfectious cause is common, but the exact pathogen often remains unproven
options.B: Myocarditis is almost always bacterial in children
options.C: A negative respiratory viral panel excludes infectious myocarditis
options.D: Every case requires myocardial viral PCR before treatment
options.E: The diagnosis is invalid unless a pathogen is identified

questions.rationale: Viral-associated or postinfectious disease is common in children, but pathogen identification is often incomplete and is not required for a clinical diagnosis.

option_explanations.A: Correct. This reflects the usual diagnostic reality.
option_explanations.B: Bacterial causes are much less common.
option_explanations.C: A respiratory panel samples a different compartment and cannot exclude myocarditis.
option_explanations.D: Myocardial PCR requires biopsy and is not routine in every case.
option_explanations.E: Myocarditis can be diagnosed clinically or by CMR without pathogen proof.

questions.board_pearl: Do not confuse failure to identify a virus with failure to diagnose myocarditis.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old child with myocarditis develops new second-degree AV block on telemetry but remains perfusing adequately. What is the best interpretation?

options.A: The conduction abnormality is unrelated because myocarditis affects only contractility
options.B: Conduction disease can occur in myocarditis and warrants continued close monitoring
options.C: The child can be discharged if troponin is falling
options.D: This finding proves congenital complete heart block
options.E: The rhythm eliminates the possibility of ventricular arrhythmias

questions.rationale: Myocardial inflammation can involve the conduction system, producing AV conduction abnormalities that may progress and require monitoring.

option_explanations.A: Myocarditis can affect both mechanical and electrical function.
option_explanations.B: Correct. AV block is a recognized manifestation.
option_explanations.C: A falling biomarker does not negate electrical risk.
option_explanations.D: New-onset block in this context is acquired until proven otherwise.
option_explanations.E: Different arrhythmias can coexist during myocarditis.

questions.board_pearl: Myocarditis is an electrical disease as well as a pump disease.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old girl had myocarditis with depressed LV function that normalized before discharge. Which follow-up statement is most appropriate?

options.A: Normalization of ejection fraction eliminates the need for cardiology follow-up
options.B: Persistent risk assessment is still needed because arrhythmia or residual myocardial injury may outlast symptom and function recovery
options.D: A normal echocardiogram proves there is no residual myocardial scar
options.E: She may return to competitive sport immediately

questions.rationale: Clinical and functional recovery is encouraging but does not automatically exclude residual inflammation, scar, or arrhythmic risk.

option_explanations.A: Follow-up remains important after acute myocarditis.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Recovery is multidimensional, not defined by EF alone.
option_explanations.D: Echocardiography cannot characterize scar like CMR.
option_explanations.E: Return to sport requires structured reassessment after an appropriate restriction period.

questions.board_pearl: Normal EF is not synonymous with complete biologic or electrical recovery.
